content.title: About
content.content: Walnuts are the edible seeds of trees belonging to the genus Juglans, most commonly the English or Persian walnut (Juglans regia). Protected by a hard outer shell, the brain-shaped kernel inside is prized for its rich, buttery texture and high concentration of plant-based omega-3 fatty acids.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Walnuts are the only tree nut containing significant amounts of ALA omega-3 fatty acids.
The physical appearance of a walnut kernel famously resembles the human brain.
Walnut trees produce juglone, a natural compound that suppresses competing surrounding plants.
They have been consumed by humans for over 10,000 years.
The green outer husk was historically used as a natural textile dye.

items.title: Rich in ALA Omega-3
items.content: Essential plant fatty acid supporting brain function and cardiovascular health.

items.title: Powerful Polyphenols
items.content: Contains high levels of antioxidant polyphenols, particularly ellagitannins.

items.title: Gut Microbiome Support
items.content: Promotes the growth of beneficial gut bacteria that produce butyrate.

items.title: Brain Health
items.content: Nutrients like polyunsaturated fats, polyphenols, and vitamin E help reduce oxidative stress in brain tissue.

items.title: Tree Nut Allergy
items.content: Can trigger severe allergic reactions in individuals with tree nut allergies.

items.title: High Calorie Density
items.content: Calorically dense; consume in portion-controlled quantities for weight management.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat raw as a snack, toss into green salads, mix into oatmeal, or chop into baked goods like muffins and banana bread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent the delicate omega-3 oils from going rancid.
